headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 cuts API prices with two token tiers
dek: Anthropic's compact model costs about 75% less than Haiku 4.5, per Olhar Digital and Canaltech.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Cheaper by tier, not by flat rate
body: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on Wednesday, a compact model for high-volume work. It completes the Claude 5.5 lineup next to Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).

Running it costs 75% less on average than Haiku 4.5, according to Anthropic. Its identifier is claude-haiku-5-5, and it is on Anthropic's platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Two prices, split at 100,000 tokens
s3.body: Tokens are the text units models bill by. The rate depends on how long the prompt is (Olhar Digital).

points.t: Up to 100,000 tokens: $0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output, down by up to 90% (Olhar Digital IA)
Above that size: $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output (Olhar Digital IA)
Anthropic says about 90% of Haiku 4.5 requests fell under 100,000 tokens (Olhar Digital).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Gains come from Anthropic's own tests
body: On OSWorld 2.1, which measures agents operating a computer, Haiku 5.5 scored 72.4%, up from 15.7%. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, a terminal coding test, it went from 0% to 39.2% (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
Humanity's Last Exam: 45.9% without tools and 57.4% with tools, against 10.2% and 18.7%. Both outlets note the results are not an independent evaluation (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).

items.t: Monthly API credits: $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, up to $500 for Team (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
The Python and TypeScript SDKs gained beta support for agents that use a computer or browser (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
Cybersecurity limits are stricter than Haiku 4.5's but looser than on newer, larger models (Olhar Digital).

caption.hook: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched with API prices up to 90% lower on short prompts, according to Olhar Digital.
body: Canaltech describes the model as built for repetitive, cost-sensitive tasks such as summarization, classification and database queries. It can also run as a coding sub-agent beside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.

Anthropic's documentation, cited by Olhar Digital, lists a one-million-token context window. Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-tier model with adjustable effort levels, which set how much reasoning it applies before answering (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
caption.cta: Which of its listed tasks, such as classification or summarization, would a cheaper model change most for a team?
